statement: Counting corruptions. Moreover, we quantify in this work the security loss by the number of users the adversary registers. A recent work [Bel+24] argued that it is beneficial to count the number of corrupted users instead, which is in many real-world scenarios much lower than the number of total users. They also present a generic framework that shows that in many settings it is possible to get a security loss that only grows with the number of corrupted users. However, their framework does not capture the security notions needed for non-interactive key exchange. We leave it as an open problem whether the security loss for our construction (or NIKEs, in general) can be improved to grow only (linearly) in the number of corrupted users.
context: An interesting open problem is how DKR security can be achieved in the setting with polynomial modulus-to-noise ratio. The work [Lan23] shows that adding NIZKPoKs is not sufficient in this setting. Counting corruptions. Such a result would not contradict our lower bound showing that a security loss of Ω(N ) is unavoidable, because the number of corruptions that the metareduction makes is approximately the same as the total number of users. 2 Technical overview Lattice-based NIKE. We first recall the folklore lattice-based NIKE, that has been studied (in a few variations) in prior work [DXL12; Pei14; Lan23; Gaj+24].
